Variable machine sizing (specs/slice-fleet, phase 1). Migration 036 adds the machine sizing columns (`memory_units`/`target_memory_units`/`disk_gb`/`target_disk_gb` on pool_hosts, backfilling units from the bake-stamped `memory_gb` attribute) and the two new plan quotas (`max_active_machine_units`, `max_total_machine_disk_gb`).

New `POST /machines/{id}/resize` (and the admin variant, which skips quotas): validates the allowed-size set (multiples of 8 units up to 128), refuses disk shrinks and `starting` rows, checks quotas at the grant point, and stamps the targets; targets equal to current clear pending targets. Gen-1 rows refuse resizing.

The start is what applies a pending resize: restart-in-place re-checks the box's two budgets under the allocation lock, rewrites the env file at the target size, and grows the data-disk qcow2 (falling back to the restore path when the origin box lacks room); restores reserve at the target size and grow the downloaded disk before boot. A successful start restamps current = applied and clears the targets. When every candidate box refuses for capacity, the restore destroys just enough unleased `available` pool rows (two-pass eviction, fewest-evictions box first) and retries; an impossible size fails the start back to `stopped` with a clear "try a smaller size" error. New metrics: `machine_resize_recorded`, `machine_resize_placement_impossible`, `pool_rows_evicted`, `machine_disk_backfilled`.

Gen-2 stop uploads record the disks' measured qcow2 virtual sizes in the artifact manifest and lazily backfill `disk_gb`. Lease and workspace responses expose the sizes additively; the lease and start paths enforce the new quotas; `/account` reports machine-unit and disk usage.

This branch also carries the earlier slice-fleet gen-2 phase 1-4 work; see the `mngr-slice-fleet-gen2-phase-*` and `mngr-variable-sizing` entries in this same PR.

Dev-canary fixes landed in this same PR: the gen-2 box scripts now parse qemu-img's top-level `virtual-size` only (qemu 10 nests child nodes whose extra numbers silently disabled the in-place disk grow and the measured-size backfill), and eviction planning excludes the restoring machine's own row (self-counting made near-budget sizes report "not possible even after eviction"). The start path re-reads the row under the user lock before its units re-check, the resize disk quota counts crashed machines correctly, stale below-recorded disk targets are clamped on both apply paths, and the admin resize serializes against concurrent starts.
